Training/Rucking plans
RUCK WITH A PURPOSE

Rucking plans

Pick a direction, build your engine, and earn the next distance. These are starting points you can adjust, not one-size-fits-all rules.

01

Build a base

Start with two or three rucks a week you can finish well. Keep the first one steady, make another longer, and leave room for recovery between harder sessions.

  • Set a repeatable distance and log time, terrain and load.
  • Add one variable at a time: distance, pace, hills or weight.
  • Repeat a benchmark route every few weeks and note what changed.
02

Build endurance

Longer events reward time on your feet. Work toward longer, sustained efforts without making every session a maximum-effort test.

  • One quality midweek ruck with deliberate pacing.
  • One longer weekend ruck with a clear turnaround or finish.
  • A shorter recovery session or strength work when the week allows.
03

Prepare for an event

Plan backwards from the actual event: distance, elevation, terrain, load rules, time cut-offs and support points.

  • Read the organiser’s latest rules before planning.
  • Practise with the gear and food you intend to use.
  • Reduce volume before the event rather than squeezing in another all-out session.

Training plans (4)

Choose a plan that matches what you can comfortably repeat today. These are starting points, not entry standards.

Your first 12 weeks of rucking

12 weeks · 3 training days · beginner

Build a routine you can keep. Start with short walks and finish with a longer outing if you are ready.

12 weeks to a longer ruck

12 weeks · 4 training days · distance

For regular ruckers working toward a comfortable 20–30 km walk or a first longer event.

12 weeks for hills and mountain days

12 weeks · 4 training days · hills

Develop climbing strength, controlled descents and longer outings without relying on a heavier pack.

Eight weeks for a team endurance challenge

8 weeks · 4 training days · team

Combine repeatable rucks, shared carries, practical communication and strength without trying to recreate an extreme event.

Build a repeatable training week

Use a recent session you could repeat as the starting point. This is a planning template, not a personalised programme.

Choose your inputs and build a week.

Plan the weeks before your goal

Make a repeatable block from your current capacity and target date. Choose a small increase in duration or hold the same duration; the plan keeps pack load fixed. Reassess before increasing work. This is not a prediction of readiness.

Choose your date and current capacity.
